# PhotoCraft
> Free, open-source, native Adobe Photoshop alternative built from scratch in pure Rust. Runs in browser via WebGPU/WebAssembly and native desktop.

## Summary
PhotoCraft is a professional raster graphics editor designed by the ArtCraft project as a clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop. It provides 1:1 workflow and shortcut parity (Cmd/Ctrl+J, Cmd/Ctrl+T, etc.), full multi-layer PSD/PSB file fidelity, 52 native tools, 16 adjustment layers, and real ICC color management. It is free under the MIT / Apache-2.0 license, requires no subscription or account, and processes all documents locally on the user's hardware.

## Core Capabilities
- **1:1 Photoshop Parity**: Familiar UI layout, menus, layer styles (Drop Shadow, Stroke, Glow, Bevel), and shortcuts.
- **PSD Without Compromise**: Pixel-accurate PSD/PSB opening and saving. Tested against 300+ oracle files.
- **GPU Accelerated**: Native wgpu compositor leveraging Metal, Vulkan, DirectX 12, and WebGPU.
- **Agent-Ready Architecture**: Built for AI automation. Over 500 commands accessible via Model Context Protocol (MCP), CLI (`photocraft-cli`), and JSON control socket.
- **Formats Supported**: PSD, PSB, layered TIFF, Paint.NET (PDN), SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, OpenEXR, HDR, and native `.pcraft`.
- **Zero Subscription**: 100% free software, private, and offline-first.

## Online Web Application
- URL: https://photocraft.work/
- Direct Editor: https://photocraft.work/#editor
- GitHub Source: https://github.com/bshx2024/photocraft

## Frequent Comparisons
- **PhotoCraft vs Photoshop**: PhotoCraft is free, open source, has no monthly subscription, respects user data privacy, and supports AI agents via MCP.
- **PhotoCraft vs GIMP**: PhotoCraft uses Photoshop's exact menu structure, shortcuts, and layer style paradigm, eliminating the steep learning curve of GIMP.
